plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds others' bids, and you always pay the second-highest bid rather than your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade up or down. Bidding exactly $10 guarantees I capture positive profit whenever I'm the highest valuer, and avoids overpaying since payment equals the second-highest bid. No history exists to suggest deviation, so I'll bid my true value.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding truthfully (equal to my value) is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying. Bidding higher than my value risks negative profit if I win at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior history, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value: bidding higher risks overpaying if I win against a bid above my value, and bidding lower only risks losing profitable opportunities without any benefit. Since my value is $25, bidding $25 ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never pay more than my value.
